sections.h2: Power line corridors pay 30% to 60% of market value, a pipeline 10%

chart.title: Corridor rates run 3 to 6 times the pipeline's 10% of market value
chart.sub: Share of market value of the land, %.
chart.source: Ministry of Power, 6 October 2026 letter; Petroleum and Minerals Pipelines Act, 1962, s.10(4).

sections.means: The 6 October 2026 letter sets corridor payments at 30%, 45% or 60% of market value, while the 1962 pipeline Act pays 10%, once.
sections.todo: Landowners below a corridor should check whether their state has notified a Market Rate Committee and Appellate Authority, since states may still adopt their own rules.

sections.h2: Tower-base land is valued at 200% of market value, far above corridors

chart.title: A tower base pays ₹140.00 lakh per hectare, a rural corridor ₹21.00 lakh
chart.sub: Payment per hectare at ₹70 lakh market value, ₹ lakh.
chart.source: Ministry of Power, 6 October 2026 letter; worked example.

sections.means: On a hectare valued at ₹70 lakh, a tower base pays ₹140.00 lakh at 200%, against ₹21.00 lakh at 30% for a rural corridor.
sections.todo: Owners of tower-base land should ask for the Market Rate Committee's notified rate, since the 200% is applied to that market value.

sections.h2: Market-rate pricing adds ₹44.34 lakh per km of 400 kV line

chart.title: Market value lifts a 400 kV kilometre from ₹59.12 lakh to ₹103.46 lakh
chart.sub: Corridor plus tower-base payment for one kilometre, ₹ lakh.
chart.source: CEA Schedule VII corridor width; author's assumed tower footprint.

sections.means: Corridor and tower-base payments for one kilometre total ₹103.46 lakh at market value and ₹59.12 lakh at circle rate, a gap of ₹44.34 lakh.
sections.todo: Developers and regulators should track the CERC Change in Law pass-through, since extra compensation can be recovered from tariffs paid by consumers.
